title: intent doctor infers a criterion's work package from its ID prefix and flags every criterion whose WP is absent, consulting no state at all -- so there is no way to record a WP descoped together with its criteria, and 62 rows a human deliberately retired are reported as residue (38% of one estate's finding count)
body:
**CORRECTED 2026-09-05 by the reporter. The symptom stands; the mechanism I first filed was wrong and its control was confounded. What follows is the corrected account, and the correction is the more useful half.**

**AS FIRST FILED (WRONG):** that `intent doctor`'s model-inconsistency check ignores a criterion's `state.is` while `intent ac gate` honours it, so withdrawn rows are reported as residue. The fix implied was "consult `state.is`".

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING.** `doctor` derives a criterion's work-package membership from its **ID prefix** -- `AC-04.1` is taken to belong to WP-04 -- and flags any criterion whose inferred WP is not present on the thread. Prefix `00` is exempt as thread-level. **No state field is consulted for any row, withdrawn or otherwise.** There is no explicit `wp` field on a criterion to consult instead; the ID is the only membership record.

**Lamplight ST0356, measured 2026-09-05.**

```
WPs the thread HAS                seq 1, 2, 3
criteria                          82   across ID prefixes 00..13
  state.is: computed              17
  state.is: withdrawn             65

doctor model-inconsistent rows    61   ("AC-xx.x belongs to WP-yy, which ST0356 does not have")
  ID prefixes flagged             04..13   -- every criterion in every absent WP
  ID prefixes NOT flagged         00 (exempt), 01, 02, 03 (present)
```

**WHY MY ORIGINAL CONTROL WAS VACUOUS, WHICH IS THE INSTRUCTIVE PART.** I reported "non-withdrawn rows flagged: NONE, against a non-withdrawn population of 17, so the control is real". All 17 of those sit in WPs 01-03, which EXIST -- so under the true rule they could never be flagged whatever their state. The control varied state while holding WP-presence fixed at "present", and WP-presence is the only variable that matters. It could not have come out any other way, and I read that as confirmation.

I also read "all 61 flagged rows are withdrawn" as evidence that withdrawal drives the flag. It is a perfect correlation produced by a third fact: **hv withdrew WPs 04-13 wholesale**, so every criterion in an absent WP happens to be withdrawn on this thread. The two hypotheses are perfectly confounded on ST0356 and no measurement taken there can separate them.

**THE ROW THAT SEPARATES THEM, on a different thread.** Lamplight ST0227 `AC-03.1`:

```
state.is   satisfied           <- NOT withdrawn
evidence   "hv ruling 2026-06-20 (reading A, display-only; WP-03 out of scope)"
text       "DEFERRED -- hv selected reading (A) ... This thread's boundary is WP-01 + WP-02."
doctor     FLAGGED -- "AC-03.1 belongs to WP-03, which ST0227 does not have"
```

A **satisfied** criterion, whose text records the human ruling that removed its WP, flagged identically to the 61 withdrawn ones. **`state.is` is not the variable.** Total across the estate: 62 rows, 61 on ST0356 and this one.

**WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY IS, AND WHY THE ORIGINAL FIX WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT.** Skipping withdrawn rows would have silenced 61 of 62 and left ST0227 flagged forever, while hiding the real gap: **the model cannot express "this work package was descoped, and its criteria with it".** Withdrawing every criterion is precisely what a careful human does -- hv did it on ST0356 -- and it does not help, because the flag is about the WP's absence, not the criteria's state. There is nowhere to record the decision, so the report asks the human to repair a decision they made, every time, forever.

Two candidate directions, neither obviously right: give a criterion an explicit WP reference so membership stops being inferred from notation, or let a thread record a descoped/withdrawn WP so an absent package is distinguishable from a missing one. The second also fixes the `status-gate-disagreement` cases where a WP's absence is deliberate.

**Scale.** `intent doctor` reports 164 findings on that estate; **62 are this one check** -- 38% of the headline -- and they bury a small actionable core. The corrected decomposition of the 113 model-inconsistent findings: **62** criterion-in-absent-WP (this issue), **22** test rows recording `n/a`, **14** dangling related-ST references (ST0339-42 naming ST0334-38, which do not exist), **12** AT rows covering nothing, **3** test rows at `n-a` with no file reference.

**Related, and the relationship is now clearer.** `0251` is the same family -- a checker reading a field too narrowly and reporting sound data as a fault. The row-kind trap still holds and is worth keeping: a criterion carries `state.is`, a test row carries `status` and no `state` at all, so a uniform lookup returns null for the other kind and looks like an answer.

Reported and corrected by Lamplight's `vc` node; the ST0356 thread is `ic`'s. The `reporter` field in this register reads `Matthew Sinclair` on every row regardless of origin. Reproducible with `intent doctor`, `intent ac gate ST0356`, and the ST0227 row above as the discriminator.
